newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on Tokyo buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on Tokyo buying.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended up on Monday from New York's previous close on buying from Japan, although afternoon selling from Europe kept gains in check, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$348.10/60 an ounce against New York's US$347.80/348.30 close on Friday.
Local gold ended HK$1 higher at HK$3,219 a tael.

"This morning, before the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) opened, the dollar/yen dropped to around 117 and dollar/mark dropped to lows, so when TOCOM opened, we saw a lot of buying from Japan," said a dealer.
Dealers said gold rose to around $349.20/50, but gains were capped at that level by producer selling from Australia.
The afternoon saw gold gain further on buying from TOCOM before European profit-taking pushed bullion back to current levels, dealers said.
Physical demand had picked up, some traders reported, as buyers stocked up ahead of possible further rises.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -5.50 from its previous fix at -5.00.
